lines.text: After Doeg the Edomite told Saul that David had gone to the house of Abimelech, David asks the mighty man why he boasts of evil.
The mighty man's tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, and he loves evil more than good.
God will bring the mighty man down to everlasting ruin and uproot him from the land of the living.
The righteous will mock the man who did not make God his refuge but trusted in the strength of his horses.
David is like a flourishing olive tree in the house of God and will praise God forever.
